see.n: Berlin Tour by public bus line 100 and 200
see.b: The 100 and 200 bus lines are just ordinary bus lines, but they pass by many of Berlin's famous landmarks. Both run every 5–10 minutes between S+U-station Zoologischer Garten and S+U-station Alexanderplatz. All BVG tickets are accepted.
By far the biggest boat company in Berlin. They offer tours on most lakes.
Offers different Segway Sightseeing Tours in Berlin. Start near Brandenburger Tor, for small groups up to 10 people.

Showing the city of Berlin on hand-picked architectural routes. Led by architects in German, English, French, Italian or Spanish. Tours from the water, on land or in a helicopter are offered. They arrange your special tour on…
Offers the possibility of a long-term stay on the waterways of Berlin and the surrounding federal state Brandenburg.

see.n: Ultraschall Berlin - Festival für neue Musik
see.b: An annual festival begun in 1999 that is dedicated to new music featuring both world premieres and music by recent composers. Concerts take place in different venues across the city and are performed by small ensembles up to big orchestras.

The city's largest cultural event and an important fixture in the global film industry's calendar (up there with Cannes). 250,000 tickets sold, 400 different films screened and a host of associated parties and events every year. In…
A festival with contemporary music and performances on issues of our time, organised by Berliner Festspiele.
All kinds of music around the city on this day coordinating with a similar day in most French cities.

A music festival established in 2000 that features youth orchestras from around the world. The concerts take place in the Konzerthaus Berlin on Gendarmenmarkt. The festival usually runs for around 2 weeks. Concerts often feature world…

see.n: Doors Open Day of the Federal Government
see.b: For one weekend, the federal government organises doors open days where most of the Federal Ministries and other governmental institutions can be accessed. Parts of the German Chancellery are also accessible, where the current…

A large classical music festival marking the beginning of the season. For about 2 weeks there are concerts in many of Berlin's music venues. Renowned international and German orchestras perform. Organised by Berliner Festspiele.
A 10-day-long festival when famous buildings in Berlin are illuminated in a special way.

see.b: The idea of the "Carnival of Cultures" is a parade of the various ethnic groups of the city showing traditional music, costumes and dances. Other more modern, alternative and political groups also participate. Similar events are also…

Alba Berlin, known as The Albatross are consistently among the best basketball teams in Germany, and one of the best in Europe. Their erstwhile dominance of the German league has been challenged by the upstart Bayern Munich basketball…
Can be found around the city. Check out BBB for pool listings and opening times.

The Berlin Eisbären (Polar Bears) play this fast, exciting and very physical sport during the winter. The excitement is heightened by the singing and chanting of the crowds, who are fueled by the copious quantities of wurst and beer…
The Berlin Crocodiles host regular matches in the summer.
One of the oldest buildings in Charlottenburg and actually the reason for the whole city to be built.

Also known as "der hohle Zahn" (the Hollow Tooth), this church in Breitscheidplatz is a memorial to Kaiser Wilhelm, and one of Berlin's most famous landmarks. Thick walls and plain decor mark it as neo-Romanesque, but with what's left…
Admission €8, discounted €4, young people up to the age of 18 free. Guided tours every Th 18:00 and Su 16:00.

Käthe Kollwitz's reputation as a social activist who used art as a means to express her support of pacifism was hard-won. Her son was killed in the World War I, after which her art took a turn for the morose. When her grandson was…

see.h: Closed for construction as of April 2024
see.b: A multimedia museum documenting Berlin's history. You can also visit an underground bunker with room for over 3000 people.

Also known as "Picasso und seine Zeit", this not so large, but precious museum hosts a very good collection of paintings and sculptures signed by Picasso, Klee, Matisse, Giacometti, and others from the first decades of the 20th century.
A small but interesting collection of decorative arts from the Art Nouveau and Art Deco periods

see.b: A museum dedicated to surrealist art.
Small park in the heart of West Berlin. Great place to chill on a sunny day. There are many great cafés and restaurants nearby. Linger over a coffee here and watch people passing by.

Once part of the Skulpturenbulevard project, this sculpture was made for the 750th anniversary of Berlin (in 1987). It consists of four steel tubes looping but not touching each other, symbolizing the division of the city.
An eerie memorial to victims of the Nazi regime built on the place of a former execution room, where nearly 2,900 people were put to death between 1933 and 1945.

Built by Hitler for the 1936 Olympic Games, this is one of the better examples of Nazi neoclassical architecture (laying claim to the legacy of Rome, fasces and all) and is still used for sporting events. At those Olympics,…

see.b: 150 m high lattice tower with open-air observation deck 124 m above ground.
Designed by Hans Poelzig in 1929, it is the first self-contained broadcasting house in the world and it is still in use today.
The building by Le Corbusier from 1957 stands close to the stadium. You can see a building that influenced the way modern residential blocks are designed all over the world.
A museum dedicated to the Berliner sculptor.
at the Rüdesheimer Platz
Historic observation tower in the forest near the big Havel River.

Restaurants abound here, with cuisines ranging from Afghan to Nepalese and Thai, plus several pizzerias and sandwich places. Prices are low, especially compared with other locations in the tourist centre of Berlin. Around Eisenacher…

The Bayerischer Platz is the centre of the Bayerisches Viertel ("Bavarian district", with many streets named after Bavarian cities), which was destroyed a lot more during World War II (about 60%). Somewhere around there Albert Einstein…

This area was Gay Central during the Weimar Republic, and it is today. But of course all are welcome. There is a diverse mix of restaurants and stores, several of which are open till midnight or later every day. The U-Bahn station has a…

In the very southeast of Schöneberg, there are daily shows for children and grown-ups alike. Projection is into a drawn Berlin skyline. Several guided tours to the obervatory daily with sky observation, conditions permitting.

The district town hall was the main town hall for West Berlin during the Cold War. The freedom bell (a present from the American people) and several memorials from that time can be found here. On the main balcony in 1963 U.S. President…
Features a nice fountain, stately old houses and a good night time hot spot. Many people hang out in the platz in good weather.

Places with markets on Wednesdays and Saturdays are popular with locals at Winterfeldplatz. Buy a coffee and browse amongst the stalls; this is a place to unearth hidden gems. Breakfast is served usually until 14:00-15:00.

see.b: A former prison built around 1850 with a haunting history until after the end of World War II (around 1955). During WWII it was used by the Nazis for oppression, torture and murder of political opponents. Nowadays it is a public park…
Like the name says, this museum showcases letters that have been used in signage as well as entire signs, illuminated and non-illuminated with focus on Neon sign.
Classic opera house of West Berlin.
Modern theatre.
Popular theatre with TV celebrities in modern plays.
Used by the Komische Oper and temporarily as venue for the Komödie am Kurfürstendamm (im Schiller Theater). Between 2010 and 2018 it was used as temporary venue for Staatsoper Unter den Linden.
A historic theatre in the former West Berlin, only musicals today.
Famous children's theatre with a light political touch, European recognition for the musical Linie 1.
One of the few old cinemas (founded 1912) left in Berlin's western city. Mostly non-mainstream European movies.

Baroque parish church (1716), remodelled after Schinkel's plans, with a new mechanical organ by Reil (2024) in the Berlin baroque tradition of Joachim Wagner. Half an hour of organ music every Thursday lunchtime.

The green areas of the park are free, so you can go there to have a walk even if you are not interested in the palace. It covers a large area and you can get in from the entrance just near the "New Pavillon" (Neuer Pavillon a.k.a.…
Lie in the grass and unwind at Lake Lietzensee, especially if you are with children - most of Charlottenburg children know and love the playground there.

The park is in an abandoned rail yard largely reclaimed by nature with trees and greenery growing around and within the tracks. Some tracks have been made over as footpaths for park visitors. The park has a retired steam locomotive on…
Do a boat tour on the Spree River or the Landwehrkanal - many of them start or end at Charlottenburg.

When the unpredictable weather in Berlin isn't favourable to explore the city's cultural gems, Artemis makes up for it with its wellness facilities. Aimed at relaxation, no children or electronic devices are allowed to make a full…

The zoo in the former East Berlin is more spacious than its West Berlin counterpart, the historic Berlin Zoo and has been open for some 50 years. The Tierpark has nearly as many animals, but fewer reptiles and aquatic animals. It…
This museum describes the procedures applied by the East German secret police. Every Friday to Monday, there is a guided tour in English at 15:00 (5€).

eat.b: Deli that serves a delicious Mediterranean breakfast.
Café that is stocked with hundreds of books to rest and relax. Good cakes and sometimes on Sunday "Tanztee" (nipping tea and dancing) occurs.
Offers good à la carte breakfast
Russian restaurant that offers good breakfast varieties and a Sunday buffet. Also a popular coffee/cake break
Offers breakfast sets from around the world and also good lunch offers that attract the local residents
Buffet breakfast and institution for parents and prepared for children of all ages, indoor play room!
Excellent Russian breakfast buffet.
Classical style, waiters in livrée.
at Breitscheidplatz with Kaiser-Wilhelm-Memorial-Church.

Delicious Georgian restaurant with pretty decor including Georgian rugs, some of them depicting ancient Georgian churches, and old photographs of people in traditional Georgian garb, and a sound track of pleasant Georgian music.

International chain with Italian food (pizza, pasta & salads) with an interesting approach of self-service. They prepare the meal in front of your eyes. The menu is also available in English and the entire staff speaks English.

Excellent Austrian restaurant with a great atmosphere. It is decorated as Austrian living rooms. Very generous portions, but you are welcome to share a course between more people as a starter or desserts. Try the brettljause or…
Portuguese restaurant famous for its mussels.
Original Chinese food, which may differ from the European "Chinese taste".
A number of restaurants in Berlin, where you can taste wonderful steaks.
This restaurant is a great steak house, serving sublime Spanish cuisine. Seating is available outside.
Great pizzas and professional service. Not a family restaurant, but kids are welcome and well cared for.
Real German dishes, properly prepared and big. Also some local beers available.
Very good Cambodian restaurant with authentic style. Lunch & dinner sets are excellent values.

eat.b: Excellent Indian food.

This Turkish fish restaurant is literally in a fish store, so when you order your fish or seafood, they take it from the counter where it's been kept on ice and cook it, so it's extremely fresh. The mains are quite large, so a couple…
Excellent Indian food.
Mixture of Nepalese and Thai food/ You can reserve traditional tables (sitting on cushions, not on chairs).
Italian inspired kitchen with excellent weekend buffet or à la carte breakfast.
A tiny authentic Korean restaurant.
Good Thai restaurant with original dishes from Isaan and consistent to that interior
Very traditional Bavarian kitchen & beers

This is a family run Iranian restaurant with excellent Persian cuisine. Marinated lamb kebabs and the vegetarian khoreshteh esphinaj (stew) are recommended. Don't forget to order the delicious tea at the end of your meal!
One of the best Greek restaurants along town. Always wise to make a reservation, sometimes a bit noisy.
Excellent Schwäbisches Food with good Schwaben wines in nice surrounding and neat garden
Serving tasty Greek dishes with a good wine selection to match. Has a big biergarten for the balmy summer nights and plays live Greek music on Friday and Saturday.
Tapas and Spanish food
Good French restaurant with good value business lunch sets and interesting dinner variations.

Excellent Italian food and one of the best pizzas in town, Bleibtreustr. 49 (opposite S-Bahnstation Savignyplatz), 10623 Berlin (in Charlottenburg, and Hohenzollerndamm 33 in Wilmersdorf. Branches in Steglitz and Mitte.
One of the best sushi restaurants in Berlin. Also serves good pan Asian dishes.
Excellent cuisine franchise next to the river, for the expatriate French in Berlin.
Member of "Chaine des Rotisseurs" with outstanding wine card and excellent cuisine in rooms made by German painter. Named "Maitre of the year 2008".
The best teppanyaki grill in town.

Excellent brewed beer. You can have either a helles (light) or a dunkles (dark). Although the beer is quite excellent, the atmosphere is quite touristy, and clearly not as antique as it strives to be.
Made up with sand on the floor and two pool tables. XL Cocktails will kick you faster than you would think.
One of the best cocktail bars in Berlin with excellent selection of spirits and a stylish decor to match.
The biggest karaokebar in Europe and they also have 150.000 karaoke playback.

One of the famous Berlin watering holes with a wide range of fruit wines, being drunk in nearly unchanged setting for the last 100 years. If the party gets started, among the best places in Berlin. Dangerous, when you come back to the…
Cafe/bar that offers an impressive cocktail list. Cocktails are mixed with fresh juices and matched with quality spirits.
As its name suggests, this bar is actually in an old S-Bahn car. Flashy and famous for inspired cocktails served by friendly bartenders.
One of the last old time Berlin bars in the area, and a great place to sit, drink and meet the locals.

Small wine bar with seats on footpath and some inside. Charming tree lined street. The proprietor and the shop look to be at least 500 years old perhaps more. Good selection of wine and charcuterie inside. This is not the spot for…

Very small cafe/bar with plenty of seating. Musicians play their original compositions most nights of the week. Quality is very high. Small snacks served but probably best to eat before you go as there is not much room.You can normally…
similar to the Maxxim, but less r'n'b music, for the wealthy people of Charlottenburg. Nice interior, plays house and 70s/80s.
Largest Latin music club in town. Dance to the beat when it's open on Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday nights.
Sheltered open-air location at the waterside right across from the Westhafen harbor with techno, house, electro DJs.
A bit more luxurious for the more mature crowd. Mainly R'n'B and house.

Named after the Ku'Damm, this big disco attracts a very young (and drunken) crowd. Rather cheap and usually very crowded with all the stuff you need (or don't want): R'n'B straight from the charts, Eurotrash party music, Mallorca…
Has some of the best Doener in the Berlin area. They have a great neighbourhood feel, and delicious Middle Eastern food in the German style.
Mexican restaurant and bar, in the summer you can sit outside in the adjacent pedestrian area. Good food and friendly service.
Schnitzel, chicken, salads, asparagus when in season. Free freifunk internet.
This Biergarten is simple, but friendly and a convenient place to have a beer and a currywurst after visiting the castle.
Alternative reggae, dancehall and goa techno club, but also theater and art events.
This techno club is located in a former factory for dog biscuits in Berlin's Rummelsburg neighborhood. It has two indoor dance floors and a large open-air area.
